title: Quantitative Analysis of Bioactive Phenanthrenes in Dioscorea batatas Decne Peel, a Discarded Biomass from Postharvest Processing
central_claims: Three representative phenanthrenes are concentrated in D. batatas peel and below detection in flesh under the reported HPLC conditions.
Phenanthrene-rich peel shows stronger cell-free radical scavenging than flesh and is a potentially valuable discarded resource.

source_manifest.title: Quantitative Analysis of Bioactive Phenanthrenes in Dioscorea batatas Decne Peel, a Discarded Biomass from Postharvest Processing
source_manifest.finding: Three phenanthrenes were measured in peel but below detection in flesh; peel showed greater cell-free radical scavenging.

source_manifest.title: Development and Validation of Quantitative Analysis Method for Phenanthrenes in Peels of the Dioscorea Genus
source_manifest.finding: Shared-author study explicitly adapts the original isolation and HPLC methods for four species and validates precision and recovery.

source_manifest.title: Dioscorea spp.: Comprehensive Review of Antioxidant Properties and Their Relation to Phytochemicals and Health Benefits
source_manifest.finding: Independent synthesis retains the peel-versus-flesh phenanthrene result and the radical-scavenging findings.

source_manifest.title: Metabolite Profiling of Dioscorea (Yam) Leaves to Identify Bioactive Compounds Reveals Their Potential as Renewable Resources
source_manifest.finding: Methods list this paper among published reference data used for tentative metabolite identification. This is analytical reference use, not replication of peel/flesh concentrations.

source_manifest.title: Skin-Protective Activities of Dioscorea batatas Decne Peel Extracts with Differential Phenanthrene Contents
source_manifest.finding: Shared-author skin-cell study builds on phenanthrene-rich peel and uses quantitative HPLC analysis. It remains preclinical and does not establish marketed cosmetic adoption.

source_manifest.title: Bioactive Metabolites of Dioscorea Species and Their Potential Applications in Functional Food Development
source_manifest.finding: Cites the original in a broad antioxidant paragraph, but describes pulp and pericarp together as superior. This imprecise statement is not clean confirmation of the original peel/flesh contrast.
